issue_context.title: Svelte 5: Allow more flexibility for `@render` tag expressions
issue_context.body:
### Describe the problem

In React, if you have a `<Button>` component, you can spread its `children` into a `<button>` and it works fine.

```jsx
function Button({ foo, ...props }) {
    return <button {...props} />;
}
```

In Svelte, we have to do this:
```svelte
<script>
    let { children } = $props();
</script>

<button>
    {#if children}
        {@render children()}
    {/if}
</button>
```
It's quite boilerplate-y.

### Describe the proposed solution

Allow passing `children` to HTML elements.
```svelte
<script>
    let { children } = $props();
</script>

<button {children} />
```

### Alternatives considered

Just keep the current syntax, which is a tad bit boilerplate-y, but not a huge deal.

### Importance

nice to have
comments:
`children` is not an attribute, and as such we won't add support for spreading it onto the `<button>`.
What we _maybe_ could do is allow more flexibility on the `{@render }`-tag to allow for arbitrary expressions as long as they end up in function calls, and allow falsy values so you don't need the if block. Then you could write

```svelte
<script>
    let { children } = $props();
</script>

<button>
    {@render children?.()}
</button>
```

Adjusted the issue title to reflect this idea.

> `children` is not an attribute, and as such we won't add support for spreading it onto the `<button>`. What we _maybe_ could do is allow more flexibility on the `{@render }`-tag to allow for arbitrary expressions as long as they end up in function calls, and allow falsy values so you don't need the if block. Then you could write
> 
> ```svelte
> <script>
>     let { children } = $props();
> </script>
> 
> <button>
>     {@render children?.()}
> </button>
> ```
> 
> Adjust the issue title to reflect this idea.

This is fine, it’s better than an if block, but it’s nice to pass down children through prop spreading. I understand if it’s not the direction Svelte wants to go, though.

I just naturally tried to do `{@render children?.()}` and was surprised it didn't work.

It think it would be great if this feature could be added, it would be a solid improvement to DX and "Vibes" to avoid the `{#if children}` wrapper

~~Just a reminder you can do:~~
```html
<script>
    let { children = emptySnippet } = $props();
</script>

<button>
    {@render children()}
</button>
```
Nevermind, you can't
Sure, but you still need to define `emptySnippet` for every component (snippets cannot be exported).
Worth supporting the possibility for `try` `catch` blocks so that people can create error boundaries in their app?

review_comments: Does this mean that I can do `snippet?.()` but not `snippets.snippet?.()`? If so this might need to be recursive?
It doesn't, the AST is a bit weird in that regard, it's always a callexpression or a chainexpression with a callexpression for anything that ends with a function call.
